title: Italy Carabinieri Recruitment 2026: Requirements Guide
metaDescription: Join the Carabinieri in 2026: age limits, education, fitness tests and the step-by-step application process for Italy's military police force explained.
headline: Italy Carabinieri Recruitment 2026: How to Join

sections.title: Who can join the Carabinieri?
sections.content:
The Carabinieri are Italy's national gendarmerie, a military force with police powers that answers to the Ministry of Defence. The main entry route for most recruits is the Allievi Carabinieri competition, which is open to Italian citizens who are typically aged between 18 and 26 and hold at least a secondary school diploma. Applicants must have a clean criminal record, full civil and political rights, and meet the medical and physical standards set out in each year's official call.

Graduates can also enter through separate officer and marshal competitions. A 2026 special course for 400 Carabinieri Marshals, for example, was open to degree holders in scientific, health, environmental and humanities subjects, with applications closing on 30 October 2026. Whatever the route, every candidate must pass the same kind of screening: written exams, physical tests, a medical examination and a psychological assessment.

sections.title: The selection process step by step
sections.content:
Each competition is published as an official bando, or call for applications, on the Carabinieri website and in the Gazzetta Ufficiale. Candidates apply online, then sit a written test covering general culture, logic, Italian language and, for some routes, a foreign language. Those who pass move on to physical efficiency tests, which typically include running, push-ups and other exercises scored against age and sex standards.

The final stages are a medical examination, a psychological and aptitude assessment, and a character and background check. Successful candidates are ranked on a merit list, and places are offered strictly in order until the quota for that intake is filled. Because competition is strong, preparing early for the written test and the fitness standards is the single best way to improve your chances.

sections.title: Training and first posting
sections.content:
Allievi Carabinieri complete their basic training at a Carabinieri school, a course lasting around twelve months that mixes military discipline, law, police procedure, weapons handling and physical training. Trainees live on site and receive a trainee allowance, then take the oath and are posted to a station, known as a Stazione, or to a specialist unit anywhere in Italy.

After the first posting, carabinieri can specialise in areas such as traffic policing, criminal investigation, forestry protection, mounted units or the special intervention unit, the GIS. Promotion follows time in service, merit and further courses, and experienced personnel can apply for the marshal and officer routes later in their careers.

sections.title: Pay and career prospects
sections.content:
Entry-level pay for Italian police and military personnel is set by the same national decree, so a new carabiniere earns a comparable starting salary to a new police officer, with additional allowances for shift work, location and specialist duties. Pay rises with rank, seniority and qualifications, and the force offers a stable public-sector career with a pension.

Beyond the salary, the Carabinieri offer job security, housing support in some postings, and a clear promotion ladder from Carabiniere to Appuntato, Brigadiere and beyond. For young Italians who want a uniformed career combining military life with everyday policing, it remains one of the most popular choices in the country.

faqs.q: What is the age limit to join the Carabinieri?
faqs.a: For the main Allievi Carabinieri competition, candidates are generally aged between 18 and 26, with the exact limit fixed in each year's official call. Officer and marshal competitions set different limits, and graduates applying for the special marshal course faced a higher ceiling. Always check the current bando, because the age window can change slightly from one intake to the next.

faqs.q: What education do I need to join the Carabinieri?
faqs.a: The Allievi route requires at least a secondary school diploma, such as the Italian diploma di maturita or an equivalent qualification recognised in Italy. Officer entry normally requires a university degree, while marshal competitions ask for a degree in specified subject areas. Candidates still studying can often apply if they expect to hold the qualification by the deadline in the call.

faqs.q: Can a foreigner join the Carabinieri?
faqs.a: No, Italian citizenship is a firm requirement for joining the Carabinieri, as it is for most Italian uniformed forces. Applicants must also enjoy full civil and political rights and must not have been dismissed from public service or convicted of a crime. Dual citizens holding Italian nationality can apply, provided they meet all the other conditions in the call.

Basic training for Allievi Carabinieri lasts around twelve months at a Carabinieri school, combining classroom study in law and police procedure with military drill, weapons training and physical conditioning. After training, recruits take the oath and are posted to a station or specialist unit, where learning continues on the job under experienced colleagues.
